title: Sandustry Demo — Free Steam Download, Checklist & Buy Guide (2026)
description: Sandustry demo guide: free Steam download (app 3490390), 30–60 min checklist, performance test, demo vs EA differences, wishlist tips, and honest buy criteria.
note: Demo and full Early Access are separate Steam apps. Confirm save transfer claims on the store pages or patch notes — do not assume cloud saves migrate.

paragraphs: The free Sandustry Demo is on Steam as app 3490390. Reviews on the demo page have been Very Positive.
The paid Early Access build is app 2764460. Use the demo to validate fun and performance before spending money.
Official community links (Discord, Reddit, YouTube) are useful after a session to compare demo limits with current EA complaints.
Confirm the dig–refine–automate fantasy clicks for you personally.
Check whether pixel physics feels readable on your machine.
Test early logistics: at least one conveyor / launcher path and watching materials move.
It is not a substitute for the full EA content roadmap Steam describes (more buildings, resources, chains, quests, technologies).
Install and launch with default settings first. Note FPS in an open dig.
Reshape terrain until you understand collapse / flood risk.
Complete the early refine / gold-oriented intro loop Steam markets.
Place logistics and watch a belt for a full minute — not just a screenshot moment.
Intentionally create a small clog, then clear it with sorting / overflow thinking. That skill transfers to EA.
Increase dig density and building count. Factory games spike late; quit early if your PC already struggles.
Write down one sentence: “I want more of this” or “This is not for me.” Buy decisions get worse when you only remember trailer vibes.
Watch CPU/GPU when many pixels are moving. Stutter now usually gets worse in larger EA factories.
Try your preferred input (mouse/keyboard). If controls feel hostile in the demo, they will not magically become cozy in EA.
If you play on a laptop, run a plugged-in session and a battery session. Thermal throttling lies to wishlist optimism.
Steam’s EA notes for the main app describe roughly a year of planned updates with more buildings, resources, production chains, quests, and technologies.
Expect the demo to be a slice. Missing systems are not necessarily “bugs” — they may simply be outside the demo scope.
After the demo, skim recent Steam news and Discord before buying if you care about a specific feature that was missing.

sections.h2: After the demo: your first wiki clicks
paragraphs: If the demo clicked: read the Beginner Guide next for EA first-hour habits, then Automation Tips when hand-carrying returns.
If fluids confused you: bookmark Water Basics before buying — wet sand shows up in Steam’s core marketing loop.
If you only liked digging: try one intentional clog-and-fix exercise in the demo. Factory fun often appears when a line stabilizes.
If performance struggled: note your settings and hardware — EA factories get denser, not lighter.
Wishlist if the fantasy is interesting but you are unsure about performance or inventory walking.
Buy EA if the demo loop was fun, your PC held up, and you accept patch churn during Early Access.
Wait if you want a “complete” factory game today — Steam notes more buildings, chains, quests, and tech still arriving during EA.
Follow Steam news and the Release Date page on this wiki if a specific feature blocked your purchase.

Buy if you enjoyed digging + sorting + watching a line stabilize, and your PC held up.
Wait if you only liked the trailer aesthetic but disliked inventory walking or fluid chaos in the demo.
Wishlist and revisit after a major patch if EA depth is the blocker — follow release-date notes and Steam news.

faq.a: Treat demo and full game as separate unless Steam or the developer explicitly says otherwise in patch notes.

faq.q: Is the demo the full game?
faq.a: No. It is a free taste. Early Access is the paid deeper build.

faq.q: Demo reviews vs main game reviews?
faq.a: Demo has been Very Positive; the main EA page has been Overwhelmingly Positive in our research pass — always re-check Steam for the live tally.

faq.q: What should I read after the demo?
faq.a: Beginner Guide and Automation Tips on this site, plus the official wiki for patch-sensitive details.

faq.q: How long is the Sandustry demo?
faq.a: Treat it as a 30–60 minute structured test, not a full campaign. Scope can change — check the Steam demo page description.

faq.q: Is the demo on Mac or Linux?
faq.a: See the Steam demo system requirements tab for supported platforms on your account region.
Check Steam input / community posts for your patch. This guide assumes mouse and keyboard unless the store states otherwise.

faq.q: Demo worth it if I already play Factorio?
faq.a: Yes for a taste test — Sandustry adds destructible sand physics. Buy only if you enjoy sorting and fluid chaos, not just throughput spreadsheets.
